theory.intro: An absolute value expression $|f(x)|$ can be written as a **piecewise-defined function** by splitting at the boundary $f(x) = 0$. By definition, $|f(x)| = f(x)$ when $f(x) \ge 0$, and $|f(x)| = -f(x)$ when $f(x) < 0$.
facts: General piecewise definition: $|f(x)| = \begin{cases} f(x), & \text{for } f(x) \ge 0 \\ -f(x), & \text{for } f(x) < 0 \end{cases}$.
For a linear argument $|ax + b|$ with $a > 0$: $|ax + b| = \begin{cases} ax + b, & \text{for } x \ge -\frac{b}{a} \\ -ax - b, & \text{for } x < -\frac{b}{a} \end{cases}$.
When the coefficient of $x$ is negative in $-ax + b \ge 0$, dividing by the negative coefficient reverses the inequality sign.
Quotients like $\frac{x - c}{|x - c|}$ exclude $x = c$ from the domain, giving strict inequalities $x > c$ and $x < c$.
steps: Set the expression inside the absolute value to zero and solve to find the boundary value.
Determine the interval where the argument is non-negative and write the positive branch.
Determine the interval where the argument is negative and write the negated branch.
Simplify each branch and combine into a single piecewise definition.

workedExamples.solution_text:
Use the argument when it is non-negative and its negative otherwise.
$|4x-9|=\begin{cases}4x-9,&4x-9\ge0\\-(4x-9),&4x-9<0\end{cases}$
Find the boundary and simplify the conditions.
$\begin{align*}4x-9&\ge0\\4x&\ge9\\x&\ge\frac94\end{align*}$
$|4x-9|=\begin{cases}4x-9,&x\ge\frac94\\-4x+9,&x<\frac94\end{cases}$
At $x=\frac94$, both expressions give zero; include this boundary in the first branch.

Find where the argument is non-negative.
$\begin{align*}13-2x&\ge0\\-2x&\ge-13\\x&\le\frac{13}{2}\end{align*}$
Dividing by $-2$ reverses the inequality.
$|13-2x|=\begin{cases}13-2x,&x\le\frac{13}{2}\\-(13-2x),&x>\frac{13}{2}\end{cases}$
$|13-2x|=\begin{cases}13-2x,&x\le\frac{13}{2}\\2x-13,&x>\frac{13}{2}\end{cases}$

(a) When $t<7$, the argument $t-7$ is negative.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}|t-7|\\&=-(t-7)\\&=-t+7\end{aligned}$
(b) When $u\ge-4$, the argument $3u+12$ is non-negative.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}|3u+12|\\&=3u+12\end{aligned}$

The denominator is zero at $x=-6$, so exclude this value.
For $x>-6$, use $|x+6|=x+6$.
$\begin{align*}f(x)&=\frac{x+6}{x+6}\\&=1\end{align*}$
For $x<-6$, use $|x+6|=-(x+6)$.
$\begin{align*}f(x)&=\frac{x+6}{-(x+6)}\\&=-1\end{align*}$
$f(x)=\begin{cases}1,&x>-6\\-1,&x<-6\end{cases}$
Both inequalities are strict because $f(-6)$ is undefined.

workedExamples.question_text: Simplify $f(x)=\frac{|x-7|}{28-4x}$ across its domain and write it as a piecewise-defined function.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Since $28-4x=-4(x-7)$, exclude $x=7$.
For $x<7$, use $|x-7|=-(x-7)$.
$\begin{align*}f(x)&=\frac{-(x-7)}{-4(x-7)}\\&=\frac14\end{align*}$
For $x>7$, use $|x-7|=x-7$.
$\begin{align*}f(x)&=\frac{x-7}{-4(x-7)}\\&=-\frac14\end{align*}$
$f(x)=\begin{cases}\frac14,&x<7\\-\frac14,&x>7\end{cases}$

workedExamples.question_text: Write $f(x)=\frac{x^2-16}{|x-4|}$ as a piecewise-defined function in simplest form.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Factor the numerator: $x^2-16=(x-4)(x+4)$. The original denominator excludes $x=4$.
For $x>4$, use $|x-4|=x-4$.
$\begin{align*}f(x)&=\frac{(x-4)(x+4)}{x-4}\\&=x+4\end{align*}$
For $x<4$, use $|x-4|=-(x-4)$.
$\begin{align*}f(x)&=\frac{(x-4)(x+4)}{-(x-4)}\\&=-(x+4)\\&=-x-4\end{align*}$
$f(x)=\begin{cases}x+4,&x>4\\-x-4,&x<4\end{cases}$
Cancellation does not restore the excluded value $x=4$.

workedExamples.question_text: For positive constants $p$ and $q$, write $f(x)=|px+q|$ as a piecewise-defined function.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Find where the argument is non-negative.
$\begin{align*}px+q&\ge0\\px&\ge-q\\x&\ge-\frac qp\end{align*}$
Since $p>0$, dividing by $p$ preserves the inequality.
$f(x)=\begin{cases}px+q,&x\ge-\frac qp\\-(px+q),&x<-\frac qp\end{cases}$
$f(x)=\begin{cases}px+q,&x\ge-\frac qp\\-px-q,&x<-\frac qp\end{cases}$

foundation.solution_text:
$x + 4 \ge 0 \implies x \ge -4$
$|x + 4| = \begin{cases} x + 4, & \text{for } x \ge -4 \\ -(x + 4), & \text{for } x < -4 \end{cases}$
$|x + 4| = \begin{cases} x + 4, & \text{for } x \ge -4 \\ -x - 4, & \text{for } x < -4 \end{cases}$

$x - 5 \ge 0 \implies x \ge 5$
$|x - 5| = \begin{cases} x - 5, & \text{for } x \ge 5 \\ -(x - 5), & \text{for } x < 5 \end{cases}$
$|x - 5| = \begin{cases} x - 5, & \text{for } x \ge 5 \\ -x + 5, & \text{for } x < 5 \end{cases}$

foundation.question_text: Write $|6 - x|$ as a piecewise-defined function.
foundation.solution_text:
$6 - x \ge 0 \implies x \le 6$
$|6 - x| = \begin{cases} 6 - x, & \text{for } x \le 6 \\ -(6 - x), & \text{for } x > 6 \end{cases}$
$|6 - x| = \begin{cases} 6 - x, & \text{for } x \le 6 \\ x - 6, & \text{for } x > 6 \end{cases}$

development.question_text: Simplify $f(x) = \dfrac{|x + 2|}{2x + 4}$ across its domain and write it as a piecewise-defined function.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Domain: } x \neq -2$
$\text{For } x > -2: |x + 2| = x + 2 \implies f(x) = \frac{x + 2}{2(x + 2)} = \frac{1}{2}$
$\text{For } x < -2: |x + 2| = -(x + 2) \implies f(x) = \frac{-(x + 2)}{2(x + 2)} = -\frac{1}{2}$
$f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{1}{2}, & \text{for } x > -2 \\ -\frac{1}{2}, & \text{for } x < -2 \end{cases}$

mastery.question_text: Simplify $f(x) = \dfrac{|x - 5|}{15 - 3x}$ across its domain and write it as a piecewise-defined function.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Domain: } x \neq 5$
$\text{For } x < 5: |x - 5| = -(x - 5) \implies f(x) = \frac{-(x - 5)}{-3(x - 5)} = \frac{1}{3}$
$\text{For } x > 5: |x - 5| = x - 5 \implies f(x) = \frac{x - 5}{-3(x - 5)} = -\frac{1}{3}$
$f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{1}{3}, & \text{for } x < 5 \\ -\frac{1}{3}, & \text{for } x > 5 \end{cases}$

mastery.question_text: Write $f(x) = \dfrac{x^2 - 9}{|x - 3|}$ as a piecewise-defined function in simplest form.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Note } x^2 - 9 = (x - 3)(x + 3) \text{ and } x \neq 3.$
$\text{For } x > 3: |x - 3| = x - 3 \implies f(x) = \frac{(x - 3)(x + 3)}{x - 3} = x + 3$
$\text{For } x < 3: |x - 3| = -(x - 3) \implies f(x) = \frac{(x - 3)(x + 3)}{-(x - 3)} = -(x + 3) = -x - 3$
$f(x) = \begin{cases} x + 3, & \text{for } x > 3 \\ -x - 3, & \text{for } x < 3 \end{cases}$

mastery.question_text: For positive constants $a$ and $b$, write $f(x) = |ax - b|$ as a piecewise-defined function.
mastery.solution_text:
$ax - b \ge 0 \implies ax \ge b \implies x \ge \frac{b}{a}$
$f(x) = \begin{cases} ax - b, & \text{for } x \ge \frac{b}{a} \\ -(ax - b), & \text{for } x < \frac{b}{a} \end{cases}$
$f(x) = \begin{cases} ax - b, & \text{for } x \ge \frac{b}{a} \\ -ax + b, & \text{for } x < \frac{b}{a} \end{cases}$
